segments.source: When sources conflict, compare proximity to the event, independence, and whether a source has a reason or mechanism to record the specific fact. Agreement between independent relevant sources increases support but does not create absolute certainty. For the cross-domain check, real distance = sketch distance × kilometres per centimetre.
Which account is better supported by the evidence given, and why? Cross-domain check: what real distance separates the checkpoints?

1. A is contemporary and reports 40. 2. C is an independent operational record and reports 42, close to A. 3. B is much later and has an unknown chain of transmission. 4. The cluster near 40–42 is therefore better supported than 90. Cross-domain check: 7×2=14 km.
An arrival count near 40–42 carts is better supported than 90. Cross-domain answer: 14 km.
Independent, relevant, well-positioned evidence usually deserves more weight than late repetition with unknown provenance.
Evidence graph with source reliability/independence attributes; compare support for competing hypotheses.
Many explanations can be represented as condition-and-consequence rules. The logical form matters: necessary, sufficient, AND, and OR are not interchangeable.

Facts: Rain occurred; The river was already high; The warning siren worked; The gate was closed. Rules: If rain occurs AND the river is already high, flooding occurs. If flooding occurs, the riverside road closes. If the siren works, residents receive a warning. Cross-domain check: a survey team starts work at 8:00 and works for 2 hour(s) without a break.

Use the rules exactly as written. AND requires all listed conditions; OR requires at least one. A one-way implication cannot automatically be reversed. For the cross-domain check, finishing time = starting time + duration.
Which consequences can be deduced by applying the rules exactly? Do not assume the converse of any rule. Cross-domain check: at what time does the team finish?

1. Rain and high river satisfy both conditions of the first rule. 2. Infer flooding. 3. Flooding implies road closure. 4. The working siren independently implies a warning. Cross-domain check: 8+2=10, so the team finishes at 10:00.
Flooding, road closure, and a warning can be deduced. Cross-domain answer: 10:00.
Causal reasoning becomes clearer when every link is stated and the direction of implication is respected.
Forward-chaining rule system over Boolean facts; apply implications until no new facts appear.

Facts: Rain occurred; The river was not high; The warning siren worked; The gate was closed. Rules: If rain occurs AND the river is already high, flooding occurs. If flooding occurs, the riverside road closes. If the siren works, residents receive a warning. Cross-domain check: a local committee has 15 members, requires at least 8 present for quorum, and 14 are present.

Use the rules exactly as written. AND requires all listed conditions; OR requires at least one. A one-way implication cannot automatically be reversed. For the cross-domain check, quorum exists when present members ≥ the stated threshold.
Which consequences can be deduced by applying the rules exactly? Do not assume the converse of any rule. Cross-domain check: is quorum met?

1. Rain is true but the high-river condition is false. 2. The AND rule for flooding therefore does not fire. 3. Without flooding, road closure is not inferred. 4. The siren rule still gives a warning. Cross-domain check: compare 14 with 8; 14≥8 is true.
A warning can be deduced, but flooding and road closure cannot be deduced. Cross-domain answer: quorum is met.
